liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Row Jimmy** (2 reviews): Garcia's solo on Row Jimmy is praised as great; Considered the definitive version; the solo after the first verse is beautiful and strange, with deeply felt singing [20][30]
- **Althea** (2 reviews): Reviewer mentions a yo-yo by Mr. Milks during Althea; Reviewer urges listening to Althea first and says Garcia played every tune with fire [28][29]
- **Desolation Row** (1 review): Reviewer hears a distinctive bounciness in this performance [20]
- **Victim Or The Crime** (1 review): Reviewer enjoys the odd sound effects Mickey produces in the Victim into Foolish Heart stretch [25]
- **Playin' In The Band** (1 review): The Playin' jam is described as otherworldly [30]
- **China Doll** (1 review): China Doll placed between Playin' and Uncle John's Band is loved; Victim into Foolish Heart also stood out [28]
- Garcia's solo on this tune is singled out as great [20]
- Reviewer says this song burns especially hot [23]

## Setlist highlights

- **Crowd chanting "Not Fade Away**: rare: 3 archived performances [31]

## The recordings

- **gd1990-07-19.118893.aud.dak5245-pzm.flac** (recommended): audience recording; 23 songs; 163 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1990-07-19.154265.mac.billtmcdee.t.flac1648**: source not stated; 24 songs; 162 min [2]
- **gd90-07-19.dsbd.garcia420.2177.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 167 min; rated 4.68/5 by 37 [4]
- **gd1990-07-19.156403.mtx.photoleon.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 172 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [7]

## Around the show

- Reviewer first heard parts on the Dead Head Hour in the early 90s, then got the full show from an LA radio broadcast [27]
- Reviewer stood at Phil's feet on night two, after attending night one [28]
- Uploader attended both nights, the only 1990 shows seen; the band changed things up on night two [1]
- Shows came a week before the band lost Brent; the uploader enjoyed the out-there space section [1]
- Taper's buddy Steve Ulman went in early with towels to reserve spots for the mic stands [2]
- Reviewer says the band kept the energy from the previous night going, calling it the best back-to-back pair seen [26]
- Reviewer prefers this show to the first night [30]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1990-07-19.118893.aud.dak5245-pzm.flac**: taped by Robert Mullen; transferred by Robert Mullen; source: Recorded & Transfered By: Robert Mullen; Source: Master Audience Cassettes; This was recorded with 2 sets of mics input to a 4 channel mixer down to 2 channels… [1]
- **gd1990-07-19.154265.mac.billtmcdee.t.flac1648**: taped by Allen Ryals; transferred by Patched and Pitched by Jason Chastain Mastered by Jamie Waddell Tracked and Flac'd by Norm Bowen; source: Audio Technica 815a Mics > Marantz PMD430 Recorder, DBX on > Maxell XLII-S cassette [2]. Also: Taper mic'd the rear delay speaker stacks hanging off the pavilion, mics 40-50 feet apart, aimed up at the speakers [2]
- **gd90-07-19.dsbd.garcia420.2177.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [4]. Also: Soundboard chain: DSBRD to DAT to CD-R to EAC to SHN, circulated via Garcia420 to abgd [4]
- **gd1990-07-19.156403.mtx.photoleon.flac16**: source: Matrix created (Adobe Audition) by Joe Noel November 23, 2021 [7]. Also: Matrix mix combining a soundboard and a FOB recording; one source was pitch corrected, and the first minute of s2t01 uses source 2 [7]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by JamBase: [Grateful Dead ‘Dave’s Picks Volume 40’ Features Deer Creek 1990 Concerts](https://www.jambase.com/article/grateful-dead-daves-picks-volume-40-deer-creek-1990) [34]
- Poster by diskunion.net: [DAVE'S PICKS VOLUME 40 (DEER CREEK MUSIC CENTER, NOBLESVILLE, IN 7/18/90 & 7/19/90) / GRATEFUL DEAD / グレイトフル・デッド / オールドロ](https://diskunion.net/rock/ct/detail/DF240119-006) [38]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1990-07-19 Deer Creek Music Center, Noblesville, IN, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1990-07-19-deer-creek-music-center-noblesville-in-usa/) [39]

claims.text: Garcia's solo on this tune is singled out as great
Garcia's solo on Row Jimmy is praised as great
Reviewer hears a distinctive bounciness in this performance
Reviewer says this song burns especially hot
Reviewer enjoys the odd sound effects Mickey produces in the Victim into Foolish Heart stretch
Reviewer says the band kept the energy from the previous night going, calling it the best back-to-back pair seen
Reviewer first heard parts on the Dead Head Hour in the early 90s, then got the full show from an LA radio broadcast
Reviewer stood at Phil's feet on night two, after attending night one
China Doll placed between Playin' and Uncle John's Band is loved; Victim into Foolish Heart also stood out
Reviewer mentions a yo-yo by Mr. Milks during Althea
Reviewer urges listening to Althea first and says Garcia played every tune with fire
Reviewer prefers this show to the first night
Considered the definitive version; the solo after the first verse is beautiful and strange, with deeply felt singing
The Playin' jam is described as otherworldly
Uploader attended both nights, the only 1990 shows seen; the band changed things up on night two
Shows came a week before the band lost Brent; the uploader enjoyed the out-there space section
Taper mic'd the rear delay speaker stacks hanging off the pavilion, mics 40-50 feet apart, aimed up at the speakers
Taper's buddy Steve Ulman went in early with towels to reserve spots for the mic stands
Soundboard chain: DSBRD to DAT to CD-R to EAC to SHN, circulated via Garcia420 to abgd
Matrix mix combining a soundboard and a FOB recording; one source was pitch corrected, and the first minute of s2t01 uses source 2
